voices.note: Rav Nachman bar Yaakov; also the author of the 7a.4 principle

props.gloss_en: the operative case: he was silent when the other seized it before the court, and only later shouted
does the court take the garment back from one who seized all of it in its presence?
baraita: the mishna's oath-and-division applies only while both grasp it; if it emerges from under one's hand alone, the burden of proof is on the claimant
(entertained) the baraita's case must be one who seized it in our presence -- which would resolve the dilemma
deflection 1: they left the court holding it jointly and returned with one holding it, the other claiming he had rented it out -- an implausible claim
deflection 2: one holds it and the other merely hangs on the fringe -- even Sumchos concedes hanging-on is nothing
(ITL branch A) the court removes seized property from the seizer's hand
(inside branch A) then if either consecrated it, the consecration fails -- it is not his
(ITL branch B) the court does NOT remove seized property
(inside branch B) if one consecrated it WITHOUT seizing: is saying-to-Heaven like handing-to-a-person, or is it excluded because it is not in his possession (מה ביתו ברשותו)?
mishna+baraita: for uncertain firstborns the burden of proof is on the claimant, yet they remain forbidden for shearing and labor
Rav Hamnuna: since the priest would keep a seized safek-firstborn yet it is holy even unseized, the masuta consecration likewise takes effect without possession
Rabba: no proof -- a firstborn's sanctity arises by itself; consecration by declaration still needs possession
Rabba: if a priest seizes an uncertain firstborn, the court removes it from his hand
baraita: animals of uncertain status enter the pen to be tithed
Abaye's deflection: the pen-baraita is a case of nine animals plus the doubtful one, where the owner is exempt whichever way you look at it -- so it does not support Rabba
the Torah requires a CERTAIN tenth; an animal of uncertain status never enters the tithe count at all
Rav Acha of Difti: the 'sfeikot' of the pen-baraita are lambs set aside for doubtful firstborn donkeys -- full chullin that belong to their owner
Rabba bar Avuha: one with ten doubtful firstborn donkeys separates ten lambs, tithes them, and they remain his
Rav Nachman: property one cannot recover by legal process -- consecrating it is invalid
the masuta case was resolved by that principle: the disputed bathhouse's consecration did not take effect
R' Yochanan: a robbed item before the owner's despair -- neither robber nor owner can consecrate it (the one because it is not his, the other because it is not in his possession)
answer: the masuta is land -- land recoverable in court already stands in its owner's possession, so R' Yochanan's rule is no objection
baraita: each takes as far as his hand reaches; the remainder is divided equally
R' Abbahu (by gesture): add -- and with an oath
Rav Pappa: the mishna's plain even division is where both hold only the fringes, neither grasping the garment itself
Rava: a gold-embroidered garment is also divided equally
case framing 1: the gold lies in the middle of the garment
case framing 2 (final): the gold is nearer to one side -- and still the other can say 'who says we divide along THAT line?'

schemas.gloss_en: owner of nine plus the doubtful animal is exempt whichever way: if it is his, he tithed well; if the priest's, nine are not subject to tithe

grounds.gloss_en: לאו מילתא היא דאמרי -- an animal of uncertain status is excluded from the tithe count entirely (עשירי ודאי ולא עשירי ספק), so the nine-plus-safek framing cannot be what the baraita means

questions.gloss_en: seized in the court's presence, owner silent then protesting: does the court take it back? Raised, argued, never resolved -- and no teiku recorded

supports.gloss_en: תניא דמסייע לך -- the pen-baraita (הספיקות נכנסין לדיר להתעשר) supports Rabba's tekafo-kohen ruling: a safek is treated as its possessor's

deflected_by.gloss_en: אי משום הא לא תסייעיה למר -- read the baraita as nine animals plus the safek, where the owner is exempt whichever way you look at it

refuted_by.gloss_en: הדר אמר אביי לאו מילתא היא דאמרי -- a safek never enters the tithe count at all (עשירי ודאי ולא עשירי ספק), so the deflection collapses and the support stands
